title: Quantization fragmentation & warmpath cost — field notes
content:
Purpose / quick summary:
This is a working note capturing an odd performance surface we noticed in July runs: under certain model/kernel/seq-length combinations the runtime shows a persistent ~10-18% throughput delta and longer tail latency that doesn't match raw FLOP accounting. Hypothesis: packing/tiling fragmentation at the kernel boundary interacts with warmpath work (KV prefetch, small-copy setup) and produces both wasted compute and extra per-request overhead. This write-up records small experiments, traces, and next actions.

Context and why this is different: 
- We see lots of quant packing/batching notes in the drive but most focus on bulk accuracy vs int8/awq/gptq tradeoffs. Less attention has been paid to alignment & fragment overheads in the fast-path kernels and how cold->warm transitions amplify the effect.
- This doc intentionally focuses on micro-inefficiencies (fragmentation) that add up in low-latency PLG loads (small batches, variable sequence lengths).

Quick definitions (how I'm using terms here):
- fragmentation: wasted work when tensor sizes don't align to the kernel tile / lane width, triggering masked lanes or zeroed tail work.
- warmpath cost: additional per-request overheads that are amortized only after a few tokens (KV prefetch, small host->device setup, partial kernel launches).

Experiment matrix (runs):
- Models: redwood-7B-v1 (baseline), rw-13B-slim (for layer-size changes)
- Quant formats: AWQ-8 (our AWQ packing), GPTQ-int8, FP8 prototype
- Kernels: tiled 128x128 low-level kernel (legacy), tiled 64x64 new microkernel, stitched microkernel (experimental PR#1234)
- Hardware: H100 (on-demand), A100 (old perf baseline)
- Workloads: seq=16/64/128, batch=1/2/4; streaming vs non-streaming
- Metrics captured: throughput (tokens/s), p50/p95/p99 latencies, fragment_ratio (fraction of kernel lanes doing zero/padded work), warmpath-ms (host side measured), and kernel occupancy estimate (from nvprof traces).

Representative result snapshot (median across 5 runs):
- redwood-7B / AWQ / tiled128 / H100 / seq=64 / batch=1:
  - tokens/s: 11.3k (expected 12.5k) -> ~9.6% loss
  - p99 tail: 210ms (expected 175ms)
  - fragment_ratio: 0.18 (18% lanes padded on average)
  - warmpath-ms: 4.6ms (baseline warmpath 2.1ms)

- redwood-7B / AWQ / tiled64 / H100 / seq=64 / batch=1 (new microkernel):
  - tokens/s: 12.1k (closer to expected) -> ~3.2% loss
  - p99 tail: 185ms
  - fragment_ratio: 0.07
  - warmpath-ms: 3.1ms

- rw-13B / GPTQ / tiled128 / H100 / seq=64 / batch=1:
  - tokens/s: 7.4k (expected 8.8k) -> ~16% loss
  - fragment_ratio: 0.22
  - warmpath-ms: 5.0ms

Interpretation / hypotheses validated by traces: 
1) Fragmentation correlates strongly with throughput loss. When tiled kernel lane-packing mismatch > ~12% we lose more than linear throughput due to extra memory traffic and lowered SIMD utilization.
2) Warmpath amplification: kernels with higher fragmentation also have larger measured warmpath-ms. Traces show more host-side prep and extra small (tail) kernel launches that serialize on the CUDA stream. Two micro-launches are common: a small alignment-copy kernel and the main compute kernel.
3) AWQ packing pattern (per-layer variable block sizes) produces non-uniform fragmentation across layers. Layers with width % tile_size != 0 cause intermittent stalls, which hurt tail latencies more than average throughput.
4) Smaller microkernels (64x64) reduce fragment_ratio but increase per-token kernel launch overhead; net wins for small-batch, variable seq workloads. For large batches the overhead dominates and tiled128 can be faster.

Trace excerpts (notes):
- nvprof shows repeated small device->device mem copies in AWQ path at layer 3/6/9 (likely alignment helpers).
- CUPTI timestamps show host-side alignment buffer zeroing occupying up to 40% of warmpath in the bad runs.
- Kernel occupancy reports show masked lanes still counted toward threads active; memory bound metrics spike proportionally with fragment_ratio.

Short experiments we ran to isolate root cause: 
- Forced prepadding to next tile multiple before kernel (pad on host): restored expected throughput but increased memory transfer size by ~5% — net small improvement in tail latency.
- Batched stitching: combine two small logical microbatches to force full tiles: improved throughput but hurt p50 for seq=16 (because of increased per-request latency for the first token).
- Disabled AWQ per-layer packing (use uniform block size): greatly reduced fragment_ratio at cost of slightly worse quant memory packing ratio -> tradeoff.

Practical recommendations (for product/serving):
- For PLG fast-path (batch=1, variable seq): prefer microkernel tiled64 for int8/AWQ and enable small prepadding on the host for layers that demonstrate >10% fragmentation.
- For high-throughput reserved workloads (batch>=4): stick with tiled128 but add a compile-time flag that enables per-layer padding at load time to avoid small dynamic launches.
- Add a runtime telemetry metric: fragment_ratio per model-version + kernel flavor. This helps routing decisions.
- Consider a "warmpath fusion" change: merge the small alignment-copy kernel with the first compute dispatch to reduce two-kernel serialization. Patch idea: fused-init PR (see linked PR#1234) — microbenchmark looks promising.

Open questions / unknowns: 
- Does fragmentation behave differently on Grace vs Hopper (we've only profiled H100/Hopper so far)? Need a small matrix on chip architectures.
- Does FP8's packing reduce or increase fragmentation relative to AWQ for odd layer sizes? My expectation: FP8 tends to have more uniform block sizes and might be less fragment-prone.
- Interaction with KV-cache: for long-context streaming, partial KV reuse changes per-layer active width; does that reduce or amplify fragmentation?

Action items / next experiments:
- Diego: run same matrix on Grace (g7g) and record fragment_ratio + warmpath-ms (target: by 2026-07-23).
- Aisha: prototype host-side prepadding toggle that only applies to layers with fragment_ratio>0.12 and benchmark memory overhead vs throughput (pr: draft by 07-26).
- Ethan: instrument runtime to emit fragment_ratio telemetry and per-layer small-kernel counts (ticket JIRA-RT-789).
- Me (Sofia): try the fused-init change from PR#1234 in a local branch and run p99-focused stress tests (seq bursts, batch=1 streaming) by 07-27.

Notes to self (observational, rough):
- This feels like a supply-chain problem: quant packing decisions (research side) and kernel tile choices (runtime) are loosely coupled. We should expose a small contract at model-load time: recommended_tile_size and per-layer pad_flag.
- Customer impact: PLG webapps with heavy small-batch traffic could see a 10-20% cost/latency delta if we don't address fragmentation.

Caveats: 
- Numbers above are noisy and dependent on transient cluster load; use the action items to reproduce at scale.
- Some wins from prepadding look promising but could increase total memory traffic in multi-tenant environments; we need to evaluate cost.

If anyone reads this and has a quick idea: ping #eng-serving-runtime or drop a comment on PR#1234.

End of notes.

-- Sofia
